A verbatim PDF copy is not a derivative work, so source.pdf is archived under the licence grant. NoDerivatives caveat: source.md is a structured text extraction of the article, which is arguably a derivative, so it is retained as internal research notes under fair use rather than under the licence grant -- same footing as a paywalled paper's extraction. DATA LICENCE: not stated. The paper's Data Records section says only 'All data files are available at FigShare', and the Data Availability Statement discusses file size and tooling but no licence. The collection is 10.6084/m9.figshare.c.7271338.v4; its per-item licence was not read at retrieval time, so the data licence is recorded as unknown and must be checked on FigShare before any redistribution of the data. Note the contrast with the sibling dataset livewire-2024 from the same laboratory, which does state a data licence (CC BY 4.0) in its Data Records section. EXTRACTION: source.md was built from the Europe PMC full-text XML (PMC12354769), not from markitdown, so body prose is readable as written. md_quality is rough because the extraction flattens the article's tables -- Table 1 (the experiment itinerary), Table 2 (the _EEG.mat field descriptions) and Table 3 (the _opals.mat field descriptions) come out as run-on text with no cell boundaries, and figure captions are inlined. Every table-sourced number quoted on the card was read back against source.pdf. EXTRACTION UPDATE 2026-08-01 -- source.md was regenerated with pymupdf4llm, which preserves markdown tables and inter-word spacing that the earlier markitdown conversion destroyed, and md_quality was reassessed against the new extraction as rough (unchanged: each `Table N.` caption in the source layout sits below its own table, so in reading order it is followed by the next table's body and every table needs re-checking against the PDF).
